label: Trades
examples: Plumbers, heating engineers, electricians, joiners, roofers, builders
bestTime: Tue to Thu, 7:30 to 8:30am before the first job, or 5 to 6:30pm
pain: Calls missed up a ladder or under a sink, quotes typed at night, invoices chased by hand.
hedgedPainLine: Most {{trade}} I speak to tell me the phone goes when they're halfway through a job, and by the time they ring back the customer's booked someone else.

variables.owner_first_name: Owner's first name if public; otherwise rewrite the line without it
variables.company: Business name as they say it
variables.reason_signal: The real reason for this business (from research), in spoken words
variables.pain_line: Verified pain line, or the hedged one above
variables.meeting_times: Two specific times, e.g. Thursday at 10 or Friday at 2

templates.name: Permission opener
templates.why: Permission-based: names the cold call and asks for 30 seconds. Tied best opener in Gong's 2024 data, fails softly.

sections.body:
Who: {{owner_first_name}}, {{role}} at {{company}}, {{town}}.
Why them: {{reason_signal}} (source: {{signal_source}}).
Best time: {{best_time}}.
Tick TPS / CTPS in the desk before you dial.
What you want: a 15-minute chat, on the phone or you pop in.
Stand up, slow down on your name, and stop talking after every question.

Hi, it's Dean Finlayson, is {{owner_first_name}} about?
_(if they ask what it's about)_ It's about the calls that come in when {{owner_first_name}}'s busy. Is {{owner_first_name}} the right person for that, or is it someone else?
_(if not about)_ No bother. When's the best time to catch them? _(write their name in the note)_

Hi {{owner_first_name}}, it's Dean Finlayson from Level One. _(slow)_
This is a cold call, so I'll be quick. Can I have 30 seconds to say why I'm calling, and you tell me if it's worth carrying on?
_(stop and wait)_

Q: When you're on a job and the phone goes, what happens to that call?
Q: Last week, roughly how many did you miss, would you say?
Q: And when you ring them back, how often have they already found someone?
Listen for: a job they lost, evenings spent on quotes, a partner answering the phone for them.

That's what I build. I set it up so every missed call gets a text back straight away, so the customer waits for you instead of ringing the next number.
I'm local, I build it myself, and you deal with me, not a call centre.

Easier to show you than explain. Fifteen minutes, on the phone or I'll pop in to you. {{meeting_times}}, which is better?
_(if they hesitate)_ No commitment. If it's not for you, no bother at all.

They: I'm not interested.
You: Fair enough, most folk aren't till they know why I'm calling. Quick one before I go: when the phone rings and you're up a ladder, does that call get answered?

They: My missus / the office answers the phone.
You: That's good, a lot don't have that. What happens after six, or when she's not in?

They: Send me an email.
You: Will do. So I don't send you something you'll bin, is missing calls actually a thing for you, or are you on top of it?

They: How much is it?
You: Depends what you need. It's a one-off build and then a small monthly. I'd rather show you first than throw a number at you. Fifteen minutes, {{meeting_times}}?

They: We're too small for that.
You: That's exactly who I build it for. Bigger firms have an office doing this. You've got you.

They: Don't call me again.
You: No problem, I'll take you off. Sorry for the interruption, all the best. _(Log as Do not call)_

Hi {{owner_first_name}}, it's Dean Finlayson from Level One in Edinburgh. I'm calling about {{voicemail_reason}}. I'll drop you a text with what I mean. It's Dean, {{dean_mobile}}. Again, {{dean_mobile}}. Cheers.

Brilliant. So that's {{booked_time}}. Is this the best number for you, or is there a mobile?
I'll text you now so you've got my number. I'll bring a quick example for {{company}}.

Booked: Thanks {{owner_first_name}}, see you {{booked_time}}. Any problems, just text. Dean, Level One
Voicemail: Hi {{owner_first_name}}, Dean here, left you a voicemail about {{voicemail_reason}}. Worth 15 mins? Dean, Level One

templates.name: Straight to the reason
templates.why: Direct reason-for-call: leads with why this business, today. Cheapest to learn, suits owner-operators who want it straight.
